title: Low Frequency Names Exhibit Bias and Overfitting in Contextualizing Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting contextualized word embeddings of first names (associated with specific racial groups) using semantically bleached sentence templates, and computing their association with pleasant vs. unpleasant attribute words using the single-value Word Embedding Association Test (SV-WEAT). The study then correlates these bias scores with the frequency of the names in training corpora.

Extracting contextualized word embeddings of first names (associated with male and female genders) using semantically bleached sentence templates, and computing their association with stereotypical attribute word sets (career/family, math/art, and science/art) using the single-value Word Embedding Association Test (SV-WEAT). The study then correlates these bias scores with the frequency of the names in training corpora.
